# Hackathon EDU public status check

Checked: 2026-10-16. Sources: official LABITCONF and EDU HUB pages, Luma registration page, and the official bases link. This is a public-page check only; no registration, organizer contact, or account-specific status was submitted or accessed.

## Recheck of live public pages — 2026-10-16

The live pages were opened again after the initial check. Luma still shows **“Solicitar unirse”** and says host approval is required. It gives no registration deadline or remaining-capacity count. This confirms what the public page displays, but does not establish that a new application will be accepted or that a specific team member is approved. The linked LABITCONF hackathon page currently lists October 30–31, 2026, Costa Salguero, a 48-hour functional-demo event, and four tracks. Luma continues to state EDU HUB/accredited-university eligibility and teams of 4–5; the general EDU HUB page still says teams of 4. Keep team size unresolved until the organizers confirm which page governs.

Luma says teams choose one track and build against a specific challenge, but the public page does not expose the challenge, judging rubric, jury, detailed timetable, prior-code/AI policy, or current bootcamp agenda. The LABITCONF event page advertises four October bootcamp meetings while the EDU HUB page describes three conversations. No account-specific application status was checked, and no organizer was contacted.

Sources re-opened: [Luma event and registration](https://luma.com/cwhw1uls?locale=es), [LABITCONF hackathon](https://www.labitconf.com/mas/hackathon), [EDU HUB](https://www.labitconf.com/mas/edu-hub). The official-bases Google Doc still could not be checked for its latest revision in this pass; the October 14 saved copy remains historical evidence only.

## Confirmed in current public summaries

- LABITCONF lists the EDU HUB hackathon for October 30–31, 2026, at Costa Salguero, as a 48-hour event with a functional demo and mentor support.
- Luma lists four tracks: Impacto y Comunidad, Nueva Educación, Inclusión Financiera, and Creator Economy. Its event summary says the specific prompt/challenge will be announced to teams before the hackathon.
- Luma still offers “Request to Join” and says host approval is required. It states eligibility for EDU HUB members with an accredited university, and describes teams of 4–5 with individual registration under a shared team name; it also describes registration without a team for later assignment.

## Unresolved or conflicting

- Luma does not publish a registration cutoff or remaining capacity in its current summary. The locally saved official-bases copy dated October 14 says registration closes October 16 or once capacity is reached. Since Luma still displays the request action, that does not establish whether registration remains open, whether capacity remains, or whether the deadline changed.
- Luma and the saved bases say teams of 4–5. The general LABITCONF EDU HUB page says teams of 4. Confirm the applicable team size before treating either as the current rule.
- The LABITCONF hackathon page says the October bootcamp has four meetings; the EDU HUB page currently describes three conversations. The current schedule and session count need confirmation.
- The linked Google Doc for official bases required JavaScript in the research browser, so its latest revision was not verified against the dated local copy. Current summaries do not confirm day-one closing time, pitch length, Q&A duration, full event schedule, judging criteria, jury composition, prior-code/AI rules, or the current bootcamp agenda.
- A LABITCONF page names Martín Yeza in a talk about problem framing. This does not confirm he is a hackathon judge or that he endorses Beca Modular.

## Product and roadmap consequence

### Roadmap checklist published after the recheck

The site now surfaces the practical gate before the event: Luma asks for EDU HUB eligibility, an accredited university, and host approval; its public listing gives no capacity count or cutoff. The locally saved October 14 bases copy states October 16 or full capacity, which is not proof the deadline remains open today. Luma says 4–5 per team while the EDU HUB page says 4, and the event page says four October bootcamp meetings while EDU HUB describes three conversations. The page presents these as unresolved and links all three official summaries. No registration was submitted and no organizer contacted.

Keep the challenge-specific solution adaptable. Do not present the saved October 14 deadline, 4–5 team size, pitch timing, venue closing time, jury, or judging criteria as freshly verified rules. The page may say that team approval and current requirements still need confirmation. No Beca Modular partnership, endorsement, or official challenge selection follows from these event listings.
